To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
actin binding to residues 718-723 is essential for CaD-induced myosin ATP hydrolysis inhibition.

actin binding to residues 718-723 and residues 728-732 of CaD are essential for CaD-induced maximal inhibition of actomyo-sin ATPase activity, while residues 690-717 are responsible for weak inhibition of actin-activated myosin ATP-ase activity.
actin binding to the C-terminal 6 amino acid residue motif of CaD is required for CaD-induced myosin ATP inhibition, and this motif can be separated into two inhibitory regions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the functional domains of CaD that are important for its inhibitory activity.
the functional domains in the C-terminal half of smooth muscle CaD that are responsible for CaD-induced regulation of actomyosins ATPase activity.
the molecular mechanism of CaD-induced inhibition, which is the first step in the process of CaD-induced regulation of the contractile apparatus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the C-terminal region of CaD, which is required for CaD-induced actin inhibition of actin-activated smooth muscle myosim ATPase, is composed of at least two distinct domains: an actin-binding motif and a second inhibitory region.

the C-terminal 68 amino acid residues of CaD can be divided into three functionally distinct domains, which are the actin-binding domain (residues 718-723), the weakly inhibitory domain (residures 690-717) and the strongly inhibitory domain (728-756).
the inhibitory domain of CaD is composed of three functional regions, namely, an actin-binding motif, a weak inhibition motif, and a strong inhibition motif.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the C-terminal end of CaD is composed of two distinct functional domains, one for actin binding and another for inhibition of actomysoin ATPase.
CaD inhibition of actomy- osin ATPase is mediated through two independent mechanisms, which are mediated by the inhibitory domains located in two different regions of CaD.
CaD-induced inhibition involves at least two distinct domains in the C-terminal end of the protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the actin binding and inhibitory domains of smooth muscle CaD are spatially separated, and the two domains can function in a cooperative fashion to achieve full inhibition of actin-activated myosin ATP hydrolysis.
the inhibitory domain of CaD consists of at least two distinct inhibitory determinants, which are separated by a noninhibitory actin-binding region.
